candidates.source_title: Rochdale veterans breakfast club receives £500 donation from housebuilders
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club has received £500 from Barratt and David Wilson Homes to help cover its running costs ahead of Remembrance Day.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club has received £500 from Barratt and David Wilson Homes to help cover its running costs ahead of Remembrance Day. The club meets every Thursday at Rochdale Town Hall Bistro and is part of the worldwide Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Clubs network. It offers veterans and serving personnel from the Royal Navy, Royal Marines, Army and Royal Air Force a place to meet and access support. The donation will help pay towards members’ food. Dave Williamson, director at Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Clubs, said: “It is with great thanks to organisations like these that help support veterans within local communities. The support these funds will provide will help the local Breakfast Clubs make sure their members gain the support and help which are much needed in the veterans community.” Barratt and David Wilson Homes also donated £500 each to veterans breakfast clubs in Leyland, St Helens and New Mills. The Rochdale club is near the housebuilders’ planned Loombrook Meadows development. Rhys Nicholson, managing director at Barratt Homes Manchester, said: “We are proud to help the Armed Forces community in Rochdale to come together and build on the strong foundations of friendship and camaraderie shared by its members.” Claire Jarvis, managing director at David Wilson Homes North West, said: “We hope the club can continue to provide Rochdale’s veterans and current servicepeople a safe space to come together and support each other.”

candidates.source_title: Woman dies at Tesco after police called and store evacuated
candidates.source_summary: A woman in her 50s has died after emergency services, including an air ambulance, were scrambled to a Tesco store on Silk Street in Rochdale on Saturday afternoon (November 7).
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A woman tragically lost her life after emergency services were called to a Tesco supermarket. The incident took place at the store's branch on Silk Street, off Manchester Road on the outskirts of Rochdale, on Saturday afternoon (November 7). Greater Manchester Police (GMP) confirmed they received a call raising concerns for the welfare of a woman inside the shop. Eyewitnesses described how she was initially attended to by staff before paramedics took over upon their arrival. Shoppers reported being asked to vacate both the store and the car park to allow emergency services to manage the situation. It is believed that staff and management at the branch were on hand to assist throughout the unfolding incident. Video footage circulating on social media captured an air ambulance touching down in the supermarket's car park. Regrettably, despite the best efforts of those involved, the woman, who was in her 50s, could not be saved and passed away, a GMP spokesperson confirmed on Sunday afternoon, reports the Manchester Evening News . Her family have since been notified of her death. When contacted by the Manchester Evening News on Saturday, a Tesco spokesperson declined to offer any comment regarding the incident.

candidates.source_summary: A youth outreach hub and day-session centre which aims to stop children being excluded from school has been told it must apply for planning permission to continue operating at a business park in Rochdale.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A youth outreach hub and day-session centre which aims to stop children being excluded from school has been told it must apply for planning permission to continue operating at a business park in Rochdale. EdforAll Ltd applied to Rochdale Council for a Certificate of Lawfulness for its base at Unit 1, Crown Business Park, in Cowm Top Lane. Documents submitted with the application show it functions as an administrative headquarters for community outreach and a part-time, non-statutory support venue for local schools and young people aged 5 to 18. They add: “The proposed activities do not constitute a ‘school’ or standard educational facility. No change-of-use application is required as the operation aligns with Class E(f) (Day centre) and Class E(g)(i) (Offices). No internal structural changes or external building works are proposed.” It is described as an “intervention partner to local schools, providing short, part-time sessions to help students re-engage with their main education” and functions as a “part-time, non-statutory support venue for local schools and young people” and sessions held there are “intended to prevent school exclusion”, alongside basic literacy, numeracy, or functional skills training. A planning officer’s report said: “The case officer sought further clarification from the agent regarding the proposed use. The agent clarified that the facility would not be inspected by Ofsted, the Department for Education, or the CQC; and the facility would operate as alternative provision, with placements through referral of the local authority. “Based on the submitted details, further clarification, and the balance of probabilities, the proposed development would fail to meet the statutory definition of a day centre. candidates.source_title: Star pupils shine as school celebrates its new name - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: A school has changed its name to better reflect the community it serves.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A school has changed its name to better reflect the community it serves. Children at the Middleton primary school formed a giant star in their playground as they celebrated their school’s new name with a special visit from the Bishop of Middleton. Rhodes Green Church of England Primary School — previously known as Little Heaton CE Primary School — welcomed the Rt Revd Mark Davies on Thursday for a day of celebrations attended by pupils, staff, parents and members of the local community. The school, in Boardman Lane in Rhodes, officially changed its name in September as part of a fresh chapter under headteacher Chloe Noon. The new name reflects the school’s connection to the Rhodes community, where many of its children live and grow up, while its renewed identity is built around the Christian vision Shine as stars in the world. To mark the occasion, children gathered in the playground to form a giant star, captured in a photograph taken from above. Bishop Mark was also given a tour by the school’s head boy and head girl, visiting classrooms and meeting children from every year group before joining families for a special assembly. candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget as Rochdale battalion's valiant sacrifices during the First World War
candidates.source_summary: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies. Britain declared war on Germany on 4th August 1914, after Germany breached the 1839 Treaty of London by invading Belgium, violating the neutrality of Belgium sworn by the 75 year old multilateral treaty signed by many nations, including the United Kingdom. Later this day, an order was sent to gather men to fight for the posterity of the nation, this was received in Rochdale in the afternoon of that same day that Belgium was invaded. The Rochdale Observer reported that 'a force of 900 men' answered the call to arms, and made way to the Baron Street drill hall. This was a grand shock, with huge crowds gathering, causing a crush that eventuated in the involvement of the police to hold back the crowd. The battalion stayed here until 20th August, when they left early in the morning for a training camp in Turton. The battalion was a unit of the Territorial Force, and was one of the first territorials to be taken overseas, setting sail for Egypt from Southampton on September 25th. They underwent training in Egypt, and joined with other battalions to become the 125th (Lancashire Fusiliers) Brigade in May 1915, before landing at Cape Helles in Gallipoli. Despite the failure of the Gallipoli campaign, the evacuation is remembered more fondly as an incredibly successful operation, and the remaining members of the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were withdrawn successfully. The 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were then transferred to the Western Front, where they saw action at the Third Battle of Ypres, also known as the Battle of Passchendaele, and, in 1918, on the front lines in The Somme, the Battles of Hindenburg Line, and the Final Advance in Picardy, the last campaign being that which forced the surrender of Germany, ending World War 1. The sacrifices that were made all of the ~2000 Rochdale war dead are memorialised at the Cenotaph opposite the Town Hall, unveiled in 1922, where there will be a service to remember the sacrifices made by all people of Rochdale, especially the soldiers who fought for the posterity of this great nation. candidates.source_body_excerpt: An empty office block on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre will be converted into apartments. St James Place, on Yorkshire Street, will be transformed into 21 new apartments. After sitting empty for eight years, developer Alam Investments has been granted planning permission to breathe new life into it. The proposal will create a mix of one and two-bedroom flats each with its own living, dining and kitchen space. To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Only internal changes are planned for the building, so it would be a ‘sensitive and appropriate reuse of the building’, according to developers. candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget: Rochdale battalion's valiant sacrifices during the First World War
candidates.source_summary: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies. Britain declared war on Germany on 4th August 1914, after Germany breached the 1839 Treaty of London by invading Belgium, violating the neutrality of Belgium sworn by the 75 year old multilateral treaty signed by many nations, including the United Kingdom. Later this day, an order was sent to gather men to fight for the posterity of the nation, this was received in Rochdale in the afternoon of that same day that Belgium was invaded. The Rochdale Observer reported that 'a force of 900 men' answered the call to arms, and made way to the Baron Street drill hall. This was a grand shock, with huge crowds gathering, causing a crush that eventuated in the involvement of the police to hold back the crowd. The battalion stayed here until 20th August, when they left early in the morning for a training camp in Turton. The battalion was a unit of the Territorial Force, and was one of the first territorials to be taken overseas, setting sail for Egypt from Southampton on September 25th. They underwent training in Egypt, and joined with other battalions to become the 125th (Lancashire Fusiliers) Brigade in May 1915, before landing at Cape Helles in Gallipoli. The Gallipoli campaign is, unfortunately, remembered as being a failure, resulting in massive casualties and little gains. The 125th Brigade went into action firstly in the loss to the Ottomans at the Second Battle of Krithia, a three day battle that resulted in around a third of the 25,000 Allied soldiers that fought becoming casualties. They then fought at the Third Battle of Krithia and the Battle of Krithia Vineyard, both losses to the Ottomans, where casualties amongst three divisions at the latter battle, including that of the 125th Brigade, where the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were fighting, were 3,469. By August, around two thirds of the Rochdale 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers had been lost through battle casualties, injuries, sickness, etc. Despite the failure of the Gallipoli campaign, the evacuation is remembered more fondly as an incredibly successful operation, and the remaining members of the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were withdrawn successfully. The 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were then transferred to the Western Front, where they saw action at the Third Battle of Ypres, also known as the Battle of Passchendaele, and, in 1918, on the front lines in The Somme, the Battles of Hindenburg Line, and the Final Advance in Picardy, the last campaign being that which forced the surrender of Germany, ending World War 1. Despite the battalion, and the brigade and division it was a part of, receiving immense loss and facing head-to-head with some of the worst battles for the Allies, the Rochdale-based battalion still came out of the war, thought numbers fewer, and were at the front lines during the Final Advance where the Germans eventually surrendered to the Allied forces.

candidates.source_summary: Baba Adeeko nets extra-time winner as Rochdale overcome Fleetwood in FA Cup Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Substitute Baba Adeeko netted an extra-time winner as Rochdale progressed into the second round of the FA Cup by beating Fleetwood 2-1. Adeeko’s excellent first-time finish six minutes into the second period sent the vocal travelling support into ecstasy and sealed a second win at Highbury this campaign for Dale, following their success in the league back in late September. The hosts created the first clear opening of the game when striker Ronan Coughlan found space in the box but could only blaze a shot harmlessly over Sam Waller’s goal. Rochdale then took the lead after 23 minutes. Some slick one-touch football saw captain Harvey Gilmour combine with Charlie Tasker to set up Luke Hannant, who tapped in a neat first-time finish at the far post past Jay Lynch. Fleetwood pressed for an equaliser in the second half and went close when Harrison Neal’s effort from outside the box had to be gathered at the second attempt by Waller. The Cod Army levelled things up going into the last quarter of normal time thanks to a Coughlan penalty after Aaron Loupalo-Bi was hauled to the ground by Kaiden Wilson. Both teams went close in extra time before Adeeko’s winner, with Dale sub Bryant Bilongo failing to convert Tasker’s cross before Danny Andrew stung the palms of Waller with a well-struck free-kick.

The Cod Army levelled things up going into the last quarter of normal time thanks to a Coughlan penalty after Aaron Loupalo-Bi was hauled to the ground by Kaiden Wilson. Both teams went close in extra time before Adeeko’s winner, with Dale sub Bryant Bilongo failing to convert Tasker’s cross before Danny Andrew stung the palms of Waller with a well-struck free-kick.

candidates.source_title: Council completes £3.3 million purchase of Warwick Mill - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developer Kam Lei Fong.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developer Kam Lei Fong. Once a thriving cotton mill, the imposing structure, which was built in 1907, has been vacant for at least a decade and has since become an eyesore, regularly attracting vandalism and urban explorers. The council sees redevelopment of Warwick Mill, which is Grade II listed, as a major opportunity to bring an important historic building back into use as new homes for the benefit of the Middleton community. The neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, has also been purchased as part of the £3.3 million deal, with plans to demolish the building. Work to transform the building will get under way quickly. Rochdale firm Winterburns is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, including 1,000 tyres and overgrown plants and trees. Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year. The council will then kick start the process of tendering a developer partner to undertake the longer-term work of bringing Warwick Mill back into use.

Company, they’re taking turns telling each other exactly what they think of the other’s town. Most people, though, are simply going about their Saturday. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers has backed defender Sean Grehan to grow into a ‘top-class’ footballer and has given the youngster plenty of words of encouragement. Grehan has established himself as a regular starter this season after being a slightly more peripheral figure at times last term. However, the Republic of Ireland Under-21 captain, who played the full 90 minutes of Rovers’ 6-1 loss to MK Dons, was substituted at half-time during the 4-1 win over Rochdale after a clumsy error which allowed veteran Ian Henderson to open the scoring after 15 minutes. “Sean's top. We're all human at the end of the day.We make mistakes.” “If I said that to my centre-halves, we wouldn't have seen the pass from Jay McGrath for the second goal or the unbelievable split in the lines with passes. I want my centre-backs to be brave. “So, he'll probably do it again. Hopefully it doesn't lead to a goal against us. And Jay will do it and Byrne will do it and Matty will do it. But I want them to be brave. And that's the most important thing.” McCann also explained that the decision to take off Grehan at half-time had always been in his mind heading into the Rochdale match due to the amount of minutes that the defender has played recently. He said: “With Sean, I just said, ‘look, don't be down because of that. Do it again. Make sure you're better with your execution the next time.’ “We're always going to make substitutions at half-time. candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week marks National Pathology Week, a chance to celebrate the often unseen workforce whose expertise underpins modern healthcare and supports almost every patient journey. Our pathology teams process more than 10 million samples and perform over 35 million tests every year, supporting patients across Greater Manchester and beyond. While patients may never meet the professionals working in pathology laboratories, their role is critical. In fact, around 95% of clinical pathways rely on pathology services, providing the diagnostic information clinicians need to diagnose illness, guide treatment and monitor ongoing care. At the heart of this work colleagues are combining scientific expertise with the latest technology to deliver faster, more efficient testing for patients. Earlier this year, the Oldham laboratory introduced new automated biopsy processing technology designed to support specimen preparation around the clock. The system can operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, helping improve workflow, create additional capacity and enable biomedical scientists to spend more time on highly specialised diagnostic work. The introduction of the technology builds on a wider programme of innovation within the laboratory, which has also led the way in adopting digital pathology, allowing specialists to review biopsy samples digitally and collaborate more easily across healthcare organisations. The past year has also seen colleagues successfully implement a new Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) across pathology services. The major programme has transformed how laboratories manage samples and results, with teams across all sites working together to ensure services for patients continued uninterrupted throughout the transition. The NCA's pathology workforce includes almost 700 colleagues working across Oldham, Salford, Rochdale, Bury, Wigan, Wrightington and Leigh. Together they represent a diverse range of professions including biomedical scientists, pathologists, clinical scientists, mortuary practitioners, biomedical support workers, transfusion practitioners, microbiologists, virologists, biochemists, point of care testing teams, administrators, porters and messengers.

candidates.source_title: Major boost for Middleton as sale of landmark town centre building completes – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_summary: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council completing the purchase of Warwick Mill.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developers, Kam Lei Fong. Once a thriving cotton mill, the imposing structure, which was built in 1907, has been vacant for at least a decade and has since become an eyesore, regularly attracting vandalism and urban explorers. The council sees redevelopment of Warwick Mill, which is Grade II listed, as a major opportunity to bring an important historic building back into use as new homes for the benefit of the Middleton community. The neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, has also been purchased as part of the £3.3 million deal, with plans to demolish the building. Work to transform the building will get under way quickly. Rochdale firm, Winterburns, is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, including 1,000 tyres and overgrown plants and trees. Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year. The council will then kick start the process of tendering a developer partner to undertake the longer-term work of bringing Warwick Mill back into use. Riders wearing red will travel around the M60 in a procession intended to resemble a giant poppy around Manchester when viewed from above. Participants will gather from 8am at the westbound HGV parking area at Birch Services before departing at 1pm. Organisers say the westbound HGV parking area will be closed to heavy goods vehicles from Saturday night until 2.30pm on Sunday. Heywood Veterans Association is the event’s nominated charity for 2026. Money raised through the sale of official red T-shirts, hoodies and patches will support its work.

candidates.source_title: Planners can’t get over ‘out-of-character’ fence - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Wooden fencing which replaced a low boundary wall has been described as "oppressive and enclosing" by planners.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Wooden fencing which replaced a low boundary wall has been described as “oppressive and enclosing” by planners. Lewis Mahoney applied to Rochdale Council for retrospective planning permission to remove the original boundary wall and raised beds to create a new garden wall and 1.8m high timber fencing at 1 Bates Close, Rochdale. But the changes to the corner plot have drawn criticism from the council’s planning department. A planning officer’s report said: “The application proposes the retention of a 1.8m high close-boarded fence which has been constructed adjacent to the public footpath at the boundary of the site without the benefit of planning permission. The original boundary wall at 1 Bates Close. Image: Google “The surrounding street scene is characterised by an absence of hard boundary treatment; most dwellings open directly to the public footpath, and in cases where there is boundary treatment, this is characterised by low-rise timber fencing or similar. “The proposed 1.8m high boundary fencing would therefore be at odds with this established character and would appear as an incongruous, out-of-character addition to the street scene which would be detrimental to the established character of the street scene. “The site location on the junction of Bates Close and hard against the public footpath would mean that the development would be readily visible from the public realm and surrounding dwellings and would read as an oppressive and intrusive form of development.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The festival will run from Friday, November 20 to Sunday November 22, delivering magical trails of fire, lights and sound The countdown to Christmas begins in Rochdale with the return of the spectacular Ignite Fire Festival. Providing magical, family-friendly entertainment, Ignite Fire Festival will once again transform the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall into a magical adventure featuring fire, lights and sound, with new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes. This free-to-attend night-time event will run for three evenings, Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22, 2026, and be open from 5pm to 8pm. Organiser Rochdale Development Agency is promising new dazzling trails and attractions to make it the best yet. Taking centre stage is the Body, which takes visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is Walk the Plank's most ambitious fire-and-light installation, from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists. Having previously travelled across the globe, from Ireland to Canada Ignite Fire Festival will see its north-west premiere. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on this dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism - the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body's functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. Bev Ayre, senior producer at Walk the Plank, said: "The countdown is on until we bring Body to Ignite and we can't wait. We hope our dynamic fire and light installation will not only entertain audiences but also inspire everyone to learn more about what makes us all human. We’re also excited to illuminate the slopes and gardens with fire and special effects, framing the beautiful town hall."

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has teamed up with new fitness centre Gymbound in a special partnership for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. Gymbound will become the club’s official club-wide main shirt sponsor, with its branding set to feature on the front of playing shirts across every section of the club, from its youngest players through to its senior teams as Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its historic 70th anniversary in 2028. The agreement will also see Gymbound, in Eagle Technology Park, Queensway, support Rochdale Mayfield’s open-age pre-season training programme, providing players with access to a modern fitness environment to help improve strength, conditioning, fitness and overall preparation ahead of the new season. The partnership will introduce exclusive membership opportunities for Rochdale Mayfield players and club members, encouraging greater participation in physical activity and making fitness more accessible. Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC founder Carl Abraham said: “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Gymbound on board as our club-wide main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. “This is a significant partnership for Rochdale Mayfield and another major step forward in our ambition to become the best amateur sports club in the borough. “As a club, we are constantly looking to build relationships with local businesses that share our values, ambitions and commitment to the community. Gymbound is a fantastic example of that. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our open-age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club.
